title: Hidden subjects and how to find them
summary: When no main carriage is visible, work out the clauses: the subject needs が, and an unnamed doer is just an undefined zero pronoun, like English "they".

blocks.text: Every sentence says that A is B or that A does B, so every sentence has an **A-car** (main carriage). Sometimes you cannot see it, and the reason is usually that Japanese expresses an idea differently from English. 好きだ is built on an adjectival noun, so in コーヒー**が**好きだ the **coffee** is the one being liked and is the subject; English "I like coffee" has a different structure.

A clause that ends a sentence (with a full stop, a connector like から, a て-form or an い-stem) is a real logical clause. A clause sitting **directly before a noun** is only a description of that noun, whatever が it contains. The subject of the whole sentence must carry **が** and belong to the main engine.

Take 選手が食べる料理をみんなに教えてもらう. 選手が belongs to the clause that describes 料理. 料理 has を and みんな has に, so neither is the subject. The engine もらう means that someone **had** everyone do something for them, and the subject is simply **unnamed**: an undefined zero pronoun, like English "they" in "they're asking everyone for opinions". It is not the athletes.

blocks.jp: 先生に作文を直してもらった。
blocks.en: I had the teacher correct my composition.

blocks.jp: 友達に道を教えてもらった。
blocks.en: I had a friend tell me the way.

blocks.jp: みんなに意見を聞いてもらう。

items: Every sentence has an A-car; if you cannot see it, it is a zero pronoun.
A clause directly before a noun only describes that noun.
The subject needs **が** and belongs to the main engine.
**〜てもらう**: the zero subject gets someone else (に) to do it. With no context, the zero subject defaults to I; sometimes it is simply unnamed.

questions.instruction: Who is the carriage of the main engine 食べた?
questions.prompt: 兄が作った料理を食べた。
questions.en: (I) ate the dish my older brother made.
questions.note: 兄が belongs to the clause describing 料理; the main subject is a zero.

questions.instruction: Which clause does 犬が belong to?
questions.prompt: 犬が好きな人に会った。
questions.en: (I) met a person who likes dogs.
questions.note: A clause directly before a noun only describes that noun.

questions.instruction: True or false? A clause sitting directly before a noun only describes that noun.
questions.note: Whatever が it contains, it is not the subject of the whole sentence.

questions.instruction: Who is the zero subject?
questions.prompt: 兄に自転車を直してもらった。
options: I (the one who had it done)
questions.en: I had my older brother fix my bicycle.
questions.note: もらう: the unnamed subject gets someone else (に) to do it.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.prompt: 母＿＿料理を教えてもらった。
questions.en: I had my mother teach me cooking.
questions.note: The person who does it for the subject takes に.

questions.instruction: Tap the person who did the action for the zero subject
questions.en: I had my younger sister help me.
questions.note: に marks the person asked; the subject is the zero.

questions.instruction: Tap the main engine of the whole sentence
questions.en: I ate the dish my younger sister made.
questions.note: 作った only describes 料理; 食べた is the main engine.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: I had the doctor look at my leg.
questions.en: I had the doctor look at my leg.
questions.note: Person に + thing を + て-form + もらう.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: I had my friend carry my bag.
questions.en: I had my friend carry my bag.
questions.note: The zero subject gets the friend (に) to carry it.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: (I) will have the store clerk call.
questions.en: (I) will have the store clerk call.
questions.note: The clerk takes に; the subject stays a zero.

questions.instruction: By the lesson's default rule, who is the zero subject of a 〜てもらう sentence when nothing else tells you?
questions.note: The zero subject defaults to I.

questions.instruction: Which particle marks the person who is asked in 〜てもらう?
questions.note: We say 友達に〜てもらう.

questions.instruction: True or false? The subject of the whole sentence must carry が and belong to the main engine.
questions.note: が in a describing clause does not count.

questions.instruction: Which noun with が belongs only to the describing clause?
questions.prompt: 母が作ったケーキを友達に食べてもらった。
questions.en: I had my friend eat the cake my mother made.
questions.note: 母が作った describes ケーキ.

questions.instruction: What is the zero subject of パーティーをした?
questions.prompt: 友達が来たので、パーティーをした。
questions.en: Because friends came, (we) had a party.
questions.note: 友達 is the subject of 来た, not of the main engine.

questions.instruction: What is an undefined zero pronoun?
options: A subject that is always I
A subject that is simply unnamed, like English "they"
questions.note: The subject is there but unnamed.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: I had a friend tell me where the station is.
questions.en: I had a friend tell me where the station is.
questions.note: The friend takes に; the zero subject receives the favor.

questions.instruction: True or false? In 兄に手伝ってもらった, my brother is the subject.
questions.note: The subject is the zero; the brother is the one asked (に).

questions.instruction: Which noun is the carriage of the whole sentence?
questions.prompt: 雨が降ったので、試合がなくなった。
questions.en: Because it rained, the game was canceled.
questions.note: 雨が belongs to the first clause; 試合が goes with the main engine.

questions.instruction: Tap the carriage of the main engine
questions.en: Because the dog barked, the baby woke up.
questions.note: The first clause ends at ので; the main engine 起きた goes with 赤ちゃんが.

questions.instruction: True or false? Every sentence has an A-car; if you cannot see it, it is a zero pronoun.
questions.note: The carriage can be invisible.

questions.instruction: Which noun is the carriage of 好きだ?
questions.note: 好きだ is built on an adjectival noun: the fish is the one liked.
